focal_entities.audience: the user at the plan sign-off, approving what the finished work will do and why, and rn's orchestrator in any later conversation, carrying the work on without asking them again

goal_orientation.purpose: approving the goal and the acceptance criteria, then carrying each later work to them

constraints.decision: Purpose: The user wants to find the file they need in their Downloads folder right away.
What organizing does: The tool sorts the files in the Downloads folder into folders by file type.
Operating systems: The tool works on both macOS and Linux; Windows is not needed.
How it is run: The user runs the tool by typing a command in the terminal whenever they want to organize; it does not run on its own on a schedule.

Guarding against mistakes: Run with nothing added, the tool only lists what it would move and where, and moves nothing; it moves files only when the user tells it to explicitly, such as with an option.

Same name at the destination: When a file of the same name is already in the folder a file would go to, the tool leaves that file where it is, never overwriting or renaming anything, and tells the user it did not move it.

File types and their folders: The tool tells a file's type by its extension and uses a fixed set of folders that the user cannot change: Images (pictures), Documents (documents, PDFs, spreadsheets), Archives (zip and the like), Audio, Video, Installers (.dmg, .deb and the like), and Others for a file that fits none of them. Which extensions go in each folder is still to be settled.
Where the type folders go: The type folders are made inside the folder being organized, such as ~/Downloads/Images; nothing outside it is touched.

What is left in place: The tool never moves folders (the type folders included), hidden files whose names begin with a dot (such as macOS's .DS_Store and .localized), or files still being downloaded (such as Chrome's .crdownload, Firefox's .part and Safari's .download); it leaves them where they are and does not look inside folders.

Folder to organize: With no folder given, the tool organizes the user's own Downloads folder: ~/Downloads on macOS, and on Linux the download folder the OS settings (xdg-user-dirs) name, such as ~/ダウンロード. The user can also give another folder to organize instead.
Checking on macOS: The tool's tests run on both macOS and Linux with GitHub Actions on every push, so the pull request shows that it works on macOS as well as Linux.
Undo: A command puts each file the last run moved back where it was before that run.
README: A README says how to install the tool and how to use it.
Never deletes: The tool only moves files and never deletes anything.

Where the record of the last run is kept: The record of what the last run moved, which undo needs, is kept as a hidden file inside the organized folder, such as ~/Downloads/.organize-last-run, so nothing outside the organized folder changes.
What counts as the last run: Only a run that moved files counts as the last run; a run that only lists leaves the record as it was, so undo still puts back what the last moving run moved.

Same name at the original place on undo: When a file of the same name is already at the place undo would put a file back, undo leaves that file in its type folder, overwrites and renames nothing, tells the user it did not put it back, and puts the other files back.

A moved file gone on undo: When a file the last run moved is no longer in its type folder, such as one the user moved or deleted since, undo skips it, tells the user it could not put it back, and puts the other files back; it does not look for the file elsewhere.

Undo lists first: Run with nothing added, the undo command only lists each file it would put back and where, and puts nothing back; it puts files back only when the user tells it to explicitly, such as with an option, as when organizing.
Type folders left empty on undo: Undo leaves every type folder where it is, even one it leaves empty, as the tool never deletes anything.

Undo again after undo: Once undo has put files back, the record is used up: undo run again moves nothing and tells the user there is nothing to put back; undo does not count as a run that moved files.

Design documents: The purpose needs two documents, a README at organize-downloads/README.md (kind readme) and an architecture at organize-downloads/docs/architecture.md (kind architecture), and no UX; the tool itself goes in the folder organize-downloads too, and the repository's own README.md stays as it is.
